newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian debt mixed, crown strengthens.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian debt mixed, crown strengthens.

text.p: 1400 GMT -- Norwegian bonds opened positive in lively trade on Wednesday, buoyed by firmer overseas markets and a stronger crown. But the market ended mainly unchanged in the long end, while short rates took a step down.
The 10-year government bond yield closed almost unchanged at 5.86 percent, having fallen four points in early trade. The yield spread with German Bunds widened two points to 36 basis points.
Dealers said the market was slightly surprised at fresh seasonally-adjusted volume figures for June retail sales, which showed a two percent rise from May.
"It (the figure) was stronger than expected and broke a trend," said one dealer.
The crown strengthened to around 102 against the inverted European Currency Unit index and to 4.10 against the mark.

Eirik Larsen, chief analyst at Den norske Bank, said the strengthening of the currency could be partly due to a disappearance of the uncertainty in the market following the central bank's rate hike last week and partly to a weaker mark.
* 2007 bond yield one basis point lower at 5.86 pct
* Norway over Bunds gap two basis points wider at 36 points
* Three-month eurokrone three basis points lower at 3.96 pct
* Crown 102.09 vs inverse European Currency Unit index vs 102.42
